questions.question: **In the following question, four words are given out of which one word is correctly spelt. Select the correctly spelt word.**
questions.solution:
The correctly spelt word is *reverberate*. It means resound / re-echo / be repeated several times as an echo.

*Example : Her singing reverberated through the halls.*

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

The greeting card (also reducing) the need to sit down and write loving messages to our dear ones.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Has also reduced'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct structure to be used is *had/has + verb in past participle*.
 
• Let us see some examples to understand:
 
 
• *I had cooked some food for you.*
 
• *They had bought a new car.*
 
• *This has given me a new opportunity.*
 
 
 
• *Has* is used in the present tense and *had *in the past tense.
 
• The sentence in the question is discussing one of the advantageous features of writing a greeting card. This is valid in the present time. So, we will use *has.* The past participle form of the verb *reduce *is *reduced*.
 
• Correct sentence__ - *The greeting card **has also reduced** the need to sit down and write loving messages to our dear ones.*

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

By the time we set out, the sun (sit) pretty in the blue sky.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'was sitting'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in past tense. The action was completed in the past. The rule is : past continuous tense can be used to describe something that was happening continuously in the past when another action interrupted it (this action is expressed in simple past).
 
 
• *Examples : *
 
• *I was making lunch when he arrived.*
 
• *When I woke up, it was raining*
 
 
 
• In the given question, it would be grammatically correct to use the past continuous tense as ‘by the time we set out’ is in simple past tense.

*Correct Sentence __- By the time we set out, the sun was sitting pretty in the blue sky.*

Therefore, the correct answer is** option 1**.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase.**

The tail is wagging the dog

options.text: A situation where a small good thing makes everyone happy.
The less important or subsidiary factor, person, or thing dominates a situation.
A person who is always happy to meet you.
Even smaller tasks become important if the whole project is to succeed.

questions.solution:
The idiom ‘The tail is wagging the dog’ means that an unimportant part of something is becoming very important and is controlling the whole thing.

Example : *The company cannot accept the demands of this small group. We don’t want the tail wagging the dog, after all.*

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase.**

Cut corners

options.text: Remove the sharp edges now if you don’t want to get hurt later.
One has to sacrifice to achieve one's goals.
Even a coward when cornered musters strength to fight back.
Do something perfunctorily so as to save time or money.

questions.solution:
‘Cut corners’ meaning to do something in the easiest and shortest way especially to save money, time or efforts.

Example : *It is not a smart move to **cut corners** with national security.*

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

questions.question: **indeed the ____________-ever such iceberg,**
questions.solution:
The structural form that we require to understand is this : *Superlative + ever* + *present perfect*

Examples – *Titanic is the best movie I have ever seen (Best + ever + seen)*

*It is the worst relationship I have ever had. (worst + ever + had)*

So, in the given sentence, we need the superlative form (highest degree of comparison) of *big* – ***biggest***. (*…**indeed the biggest-ever such iceberg,…*****)**

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

questions.question: **shelf, now __________ official iceberg**
questions.solution:
‘A’/ ‘An’ are articles having the same meaning used for singular nouns. We use ‘a’ in front of consonant sounds and ‘an’ before vowel sounds.

 In English alphabets, A ,E, I, O and U are vowels and the rest are consonants. Thus, we have : a girl, a boy, an apple, an orange etc.

In the given sentence, *official* starts with a vowel sound. So, the most appropriate article would be *an* (*shelf, now **an** official iceberg*…)

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

questions.question: **and 300 feet ________. By January 2017**
questions.solution:
*Width *is the measure used to indicate how wide something is. The following example will help us to

understand how these words differ in their usage.

*This table is 1 metre wide / The width of this table is 1 metre.*

Similar is the case with *length *and *long : This table is 1 metre long / The length of this table is 1*

*metre.*

So, looking at the given context, the most appropriate word is *wide* (*and 300 feet **wide**. By January 2017…)*.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

questions.question: **was growing _________. By 2016 the**
questions.solution:
Adverbs describe how, when or where an action takes place. These are describing words of verbs. They often end with –ly.

*For example, Ramesh does his job sincerely*. Here, *sincerely *describes how Ramesh does his job. So, *sincerely* is an adverb.

Similarly, in the question, we need an adverb that will describe the verb ‘growing’. *Steadily *seems an appropriate answer. (*was growing steadily. By 2016 the …*)

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

questions.question: **Administration (NASA) working _______ satellite data tracking**
questions.solution:
The correct preposition to be used here is *with* – you work with something.

When we use *with* in the blank, the part of the sentence is logically and grammatically correct : ***Administration (NASA) working with satellite data tracking***

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

questions.question: **In the following question, a word has been written in four different ways out of which only one is correctly spelt. Select the correctly spelt word.**
questions.solution:
The correctly spelt word is ‘Ceiling’. Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

"I before E, except after C" is the general rule to be followed. We often have *-ei* after c in spellings. For other words, *-ie* is used. 

Examples: *relieve, receive, fierce, friend, conceive*

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

“My hour has come.” thought the king.

options.text: The king thought that his hour had come.
His hour had come thought the king.
The king thought that his hour had came.
The king wondered if his hour has come.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'The king thought that his hour had come.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In Direct speech, the message is conveyed in the words of the author or concerned person.
 
• In Indirect speech, the message is conveyed in our words. 
 
• When we convert Direct speech to Indirect speech, we omit the inverted commas. Also, the conjunction *that *is added before introducing the words spoken between quotation marks (“…”).
 
• Some notable changes that are made while doing the conversion from Direct to Indirect is :
 
 
• am --> was
 
• is --> was
 
• has --> had
 
• have been to --> had been to
 
 
 
• So, *has* in the given sentence of the question should be converted to *had*.

***So the correct sentence is-** The king thought that his hour had come.*

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1.**

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

The fans invited the cricketer.

options.text: The cricketer was invited by the fans.
The cricketer received an invitation by the fans.
The cricketer is invited by the fans.
The cricketer was invite by the fans.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'The cricketer was invited by the fans.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When the subject performs the action – it is Active Voice.
 
• When the subject is being acted upon by the verb – it is Passive Voice.
 
• We should change the sequence of the subject and the object (or the action) while keeping the meaning intact.
 
• In Active voice – Subject + verb + object is the sequence.
 
• In Passive voice – Object + verb + Subject is the sequence.
 
• (Subject is someone that works on the object)
 
• In the given sentence, 'the fans' is the subject because they are doing an action. They are inviting. The action is done on the object which is the cricketer here. So, the sentence in the question is in its Active Voice.

To change it into passive voice, the sentence should begin with the object ‘The cricketer’.

 
• Verbs are also changed. Some conversions are :
 
 
• Eats --> is eaten
 
• Is cleaning --> is being cleaned
 
• Will clean --> will be cleaned
 
• Destroyed --> was destroyed
 
 

**Following these thumb rules, the same sentence in the passive voice is ***The cricketer was invited by the fans.*

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1.**

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

Climatic information can

P : be obtained through an

Q : in tree growth

R : understanding of changes
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'PRQ'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The first part of the sequence can be P as it continues the thought flow. ‘Climatic information can be obtained through an…’ seems logically sound.
 
• Now, we need to know through what climatic information can be obtained? This is answered by part R. So, R can follow with Q as the ending part of the sentence. The right sequence is **PRQ**.

*Climatic information can be obtained through an understanding of changes in tree growth*

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.**

Effervescent
questions.solution:
The word *Effervescent *means lively, marked by high spirits or excitement.

Let us look into the meaning of the difficult words:

Stale – not fresh, not enthusiastic, bored

Resilient - able to withstand and recover quickly from difficult conditions

We find that the word *stale *expresses the opposite meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence ****given**** with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

The many ______ of Dalhousie have made it popular among tourists.
questions.solution:
The correct word is ‘**attractions**’ as it suits the given context. Here, it means the aspects or features that make something interesting.

Complete sentence: *The many **attractions **(interesting features) of Dalhousie have made it popular among tourists.*

The correct answer is **option 2.**

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

This is Hrithik Roshan’s autograph, ______?
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is Isn't it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

 
• In the above-given sentence, isn't it will be used.
 
• It is a usual practice to state something and then end the sentence with a question asking for confirmation.
 
• Consider the sentence, “It is hot, isn’t it?”. The part “isn’t it?” is called a question tag.
 
• The general rules of using a question tag are:
 
• Finish the negative statement using a positive question tag.
 
• Examples:-
 
 
• *They are not going to the mall, are they?*
 
• *Swati can’t sing, can she?*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

The truth is that when people seeing you zoned into your work and (1)/ in harmony with yourself, (2)/ they come to distract you. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The error lies in part 1 of the sentence. Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

Looking at the structure of the sentence, *see *should replace *seeing* to make the sentence grammatically correct. The context uses the simple present tense.

__Correct Sentence__ - *The truth is that when people **see** you zoned into your work and in harmony with yourself, they come to distract you*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

The excessive use of pesticides (1)/ has negatively (2)/ effected soil output. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The error lies in part 3 of the sentence. Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

Let us understand the meanings of the words *affect *and *effect.*

The word *affect* is used as a verb only. We can use *effect* as both verb and noun.

**Affect **means to influence something or someone. **Effect**, when used as a noun, means the result of an influence. When used as a verb, effect means to bring about or cause something to occur.

Examples –

*The harmful effects of a bad company should be highlighted among teenagers. (effect as noun)*

*The bad company has affected him severely.*

*The government was not able to effect any social change. (effect as a verb - meaning the government was not able to bring about any social change)*

In the given sentence, *affected *should replace the word *effected* to make the sentence grammatically correct.

__Correct Sentence__ - The excessive use of pesticides has negatively affected soil output.
